$schema_comment: Canonical Galhoom Labs product map. Agents MUST read this before creating or placing any Labs repo. CI validates profile/README.md against this file.
promise: Real products people can use — not a learning path.

sibling_org.promise: Learn and progress — practice / applied projects to grow.

in: CLIs and helper tools people run
Any other real product people can use
out_for_now: Reusable libraries / packages as a category

categories.name: Apps
categories.role: Web, mobile, or desktop applications people use.

categories.name: Tools & extensions
categories.role: CLIs, browser extensions, generators, bots, helpers people run.

categories.name: More products
categories.role: Games and other usable products that are not a clear App or Tool.

placement_algorithm: 1. Confirm the pitch is use-this (real product), not study-this / practice-only.
2. Classify into exactly one category using category.role (Apps / Tools & extensions / More products).
3. Never invent a 4th category or reorder 1–3 without updating this registry first and explicit human approval.
4. Assign the next ID in that category: max existing M for category N → new id N.(M+1).
5. Update labs-registry.json FIRST, then profile/README.md, then Galhoom22 Labs section if the map would otherwise lie.
6. Run scripts/validate_labs.py locally (or wait for CI) before considering the change done.
7. New repos start with status draft or building unless the human explicitly sets shipped.
8. Do not add libraries or templates categories unless the human expands scope.out_for_now.
forbidden: Adding a product to the org profile without an ID in this registry (once repos exist)
Placing a Path practice / study repo in Labs
Placing a real Labs product under galhoom-path Track 5
Adding Libraries or Templates as categories without an explicit human decision
Skipping the registry and only editing profile/README.md
Changing Mermaid visual style (TB + classDef) without an explicit human request
